newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian shares seen well supported after drop.
newsitem.headline: Belgian shares seen well supported after drop.

text.p: Belgian shares were expected to remain well supported after bouncing back from initial losses on Tuesday sparked by an overnight fall of 2.5 pct on Wall Street.

Traders said, however, they did not expect the market to recoup all its losses until it became clear whether New York would move lower again in the coming days, or whether the move was -- as some expected -- a one-off correction.

By around 0845 GMT, the Bel-20 index of twenty blue chips was 0.46 percent weaker at 2,340.80 points, well off its lows around 2,330 points hit at the start of trade. Thirteen issues were lower, one was unchanged and six were positive.

The trigger for Wall Street's losses was a suggestion by Japan's prime minister that the country could sell off some of its U.S. Treasuries and buy gold instead if the U.S. again resorted to using the dollar as a trade weapon.
Belgian dealers said, however, the latest U.S.-Japan tensions did nothing to change stock-friendly fundamentals in Europe.

"We are still in a low-inflation, low-interest rate environment. There's not much alternative to stocks," Yves Kanarek of Smeets, Verbaet said. "We had some profit taking last week. There's no reason to panic."
Kanarek saw the market consolidating at slightly lower levels. "People will want to see what the reaction will be in New York today and in the coming days."

The biggest losers on Tuesday continued to be Belgium's banks, extending losses made on Monday as merger speculation waned. BBL was down 150 francs, or 1.61 percent, at 9,190 francs, and Kredietbank fell 100 francs to 14,100 francs. KB parent company Almanij was also lower, losing 1.80 percent to 16,350 francs.
Dexia CC, which pays a 87.75 franc net dividend on Wednesday, was unchanged at 3,890 francs.
On the upside, supermarket group Delhaize continued to benefit from news of joint ventures in Asia, rising 30 francs to 1,890 francs.
Insurer Royale Belge was also up 85 francs at 10,025 francs. Royale Belge remains supported by the prospect it could be sold by parent company AXA-UAP.
